concept_name: Atomic Orbitals: s, p and d Shapes Are Regions of Probability, Not Paths
source_book: NCERT Chemistry Class 11, Ch.2 'Structure of Atom', §2.6 — the quantum mechanical model: shapes of s, p and d atomic orbitals, radial and angular nodes — chapter-index scope reference only (retained in full post-2023 rationalisation); teaching, sequence, and phrasing authored from first principles. Every shape/radius/node/energy number is derived directly from the exact hydrogenic radial functions R_nl(rho) and angular factors |Y_lm|^2, independently re-derived by numerical integration and bisection, never accepted on the engine's word alone. NCERT Exemplar Ch.2 consulted for misconception beliefs only (orbit-vs-orbital confusion); no problem text, figure, or worked example imported. Fourth chemistry concept through the pipeline, first on the field_3d orbital_shapes surface (P2 slice).

real_world_anchor.primary: The atom icon — a nucleus with electrons on crossing ellipses — appears on science logos, apps, and classroom posters everywhere on Earth, and it is wrong. In 2013 physicists photographed a hydrogen atom's actual electron cloud with a quantum microscope: the photograph shows these lobes and shells, not orbits. The student is about to see what the photograph sees.
real_world_anchor.secondary: Orbital shapes are why molecules have shapes at all — water bends at 104.5° because oxygen's orbitals point in specific directions. Shape at the atom's scale becomes shape at the molecule's scale, which becomes everything chemistry does.

dots.name: number of position measurements shown (dot-swarm size)

spin.name: turn speed — the slow rotation that lets the 3D shape be read

probe.name: probe-plane position along the active lobe's own axis, as a fraction of its tip radius

pm_per_unit.name: frame scale — the ONE declared constant converting real pm to world units

r90_2p_tip.name: 2p lobe tip length at the 90% boundary

r90_2p_width.name: 2p lobe maximum width at the 90% boundary

r50_2p_tip.name: 2p lobe tip length at the 50% boundary (STATE_5's slimmer, countable contour)

r50_2p_width.name: 2p lobe maximum width at the 50% boundary

r90_3d_tip.name: 3d_xy lobe tip length at the 90% boundary

occupancy_pct.formula: measured fraction of the active dot sample lying inside the drawn boundary surface, at the state's active enclosure key (0.9, 0.7 or 0.5) — never asserted, always counted from the sample

psi2_at_probe.formula: normalised |psi|^2 at the probe plane's position, relative to the orbital's own peak density

dots_in_slice.formula: count of sampled measurement dots lying within a thin slab centred on the probe plane

formulas.energy_rule: E_n = -13.6 / n^2 eV (Z = 1, hydrogenic) — must agree bit-for-bit with bohr_model_energy_levels
formulas.node_rule: angular nodes = l; radial nodes = n - l - 1
formulas.boundary_definition: the boundary surface encloses the enclosure fraction (90%, 70% or 50%) of the ACTUAL measured dot sample — never asserted, always measured
formulas.degeneracy_2p: the three 2p orbitals are degenerate for ANY atom (rotational symmetry of the p subshell)
formulas.degeneracy_scope_note: 2s-vs-2p degeneracy is a ONE-ELECTRON (hydrogenic) accident only, and is never claimed as a general atomic fact in this concept

constraints: Every rendered radius, node position, and energy is COMPUTED from the exact hydrogenic R_nl(rho) and |Y_lm|^2 functions at build time — never a typed-in number.

The occupancy HUD is MEASURED from the actual dot sample at the state's active enclosure key: ~90% at enclosure 0.9, ~70% at 0.7, ~50% at 0.5 (STATE_5) — never a fixed 90% regardless of which contour is drawn.

At the true nodal plane/shell, BOTH |psi|^2 and the dots-in-slice count read exactly 0 (STATE_4 at the node on the 2p axis; STATE_7's cutaway through the 2s shell at rho = 2, r = 2a0 = 106 pm) — any non-zero reading there is a defect, not a rounding artifact.
Node counts satisfy angular = l, radial = n - l - 1 for every orbital shown: 1s(0,0), 2s(0,1), 2p(1,0), 3d_xy(2,0).
E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV for every orbital, and the n=1/2/3 values (-13.60/-3.40/-1.51 eV) are bit-for-bit identical to bohr_model_energy_levels.

Degeneracy scope: the three 2p orbitals are degenerate for ANY atom (rotational symmetry); 2s-vs-2p degeneracy is a ONE-ELECTRON (hydrogenic) accident only and is never asserted as a general atomic fact in this concept.

aha_moment.statement: Thousands of measurements never land on the orbit — they build a cloud instead.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: the believed orbit runs alone, then position-measurement flashes land scattered, never on the ring, while the ring fades and the dot cloud it never predicted takes its place

STATE_1.title: The electron has no path — measurements build a cloud instead

scene_composition.text: measurements land — never on the ring
together: a cloud, not a path

misconception_watch.belief: The electron travels a circular path around the nucleus, like a tiny planet orbiting a star.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The believed orbit runs for the first few seconds; then position-measurement flashes land, scattered, never once on that ring, while the ring itself fades to nothing.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: There is no path to travel — thousands of position measurements build a cloud instead, and the cloud is the whole truth.

tts_sentences.text_en: This is the picture everyone already carries: an electron circling the nucleus on a fixed path, like a tiny planet.
Watch it run, then watch position measurements land, one by one, and never once on that ring.
Together, the measurements build a cloud, not a path at all.

STATE_2.title: The orbital = the region holding ~90% of the finds; density is the whole truth

tts_sentences.text_en: That cloud has a name: the orbital, not an orbit, a region.
Its boundary is the region holding ninety percent of every measurement; everything past it is rare.
Turn it. The shape holds; only the view changes.
Add more measurements and the cloud only gets clearer; the density was always the whole truth.

STATE_3.title: The second shape family: two lobes along one axis

scene_composition.text: a different shape: the p orbital
two lobes, nothing at the centre

tts_sentences.text_en: A different shape now: the p orbital.
Two lobes grow outward from the nucleus along one axis, with nothing at the centre.
This is the shape behind every dumbbell drawing you have seen, now genuinely three-dimensional.

STATE_4.title: A plane of exactly zero probability separates the lobes

scene_composition.text: a probe sweeps through the gap
dots land on both sides at once

misconception_watch.belief: The electron is a tiny ball that must physically cross the middle to get from one lobe to the other.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The probe reads |ψ|² = 0.00 and the dots-in-slice count reads exactly 0 at the plane, while measurement dots keep landing on both lobes at once.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: A standing wave has no journey between its crests — there is no path picture left to cross, so there is nothing to cross with.

tts_sentences.text_en: Sweep a plane through the gap between the lobes and watch the reading cross the middle.
There, the probability density reads exactly zero, and so does the count of measurements; nothing is ever found on that plane.
Dots keep landing on both sides at once, because a standing wave has no journey between its crests.

STATE_5.title: 2pₓ, 2p_y, 2p_z — same shape, three perpendicular axes, same energy

misconception_watch.belief: The three 2p orbitals are stacked or nested inside each other, like three separate rings drawn around the same point.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: All three are drawn on one shared set of axes, appearing one axis at a time, and every pair reads exactly ninety degrees apart with equal energy.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The three 2p orbitals are three directions of the same idea on one atom, not three objects nested one inside another.

tts_sentences.text_en: Three p orbitals live on the same atom, one on each axis, drawn here at a smaller, easier-to-count boundary.
Same shape, same size, each pointing along x, y, or z, and every pair sits at exactly ninety degrees.
All three share the same energy, not stacked inside each other; three directions of one idea.

STATE_6.title: The third family: four lobes between the axes, two node planes

scene_composition.text: they grow between x and y
two invisible planes now cut it

tts_sentences.text_en: A third shape: four lobes, not two.
They do not sit on the axes at all; they grow in the gaps between x and y, while the axis-aligned p orbitals fade to ghosts.
Two invisible planes now cut the shape, not one.

STATE_7.title: Bigger shell, hidden node: 2s = same sphere, larger, with a spherical node shell inside

scene_composition.text: the same s shape, one size up
n survives; the orbit does not

tts_sentences.text_en: The same s shape, one size up: 2s.
Watch it grow larger than 1s, then a clipping plane reveals what hides inside.
A whole empty shell sits inside; zero probability at one fixed radius, electron density on both sides.
The level number n survives from the ladder you already met; only the orbit is gone.

STATE_8.title: Counting nodes: angular = l, radial = n − l − 1

tts_sentences.text_en: One simple rule counts every node.
The angular nodes equal the shape number l: s is zero, p is one, d is two.
The radial nodes equal the level number n, minus the shape number l, minus one; watch the count tick through 1s, 2s, 2p, and 3d.

STATE_9.title: Explore — pick an orbital, sweep the probe, turn it

tts_sentences.text_en: Now it's yours. Pick an orbital, sweep the probe, and turn it however you like.

orbital_shapes.formula: angular nodes = l · radial = n − l − 1

STATE_9.caption: All yours

regeneration_variants.label: Same probability-cloud idea, a heavier atom's outer orbital (sodium's 3s, not hydrogen's 1s)
regeneration_variants.physical_world: Sodium's outermost electron sits in a 3s orbital — same spherical probability cloud, same radial-node counting rule (n − l − 1 = 2 radial nodes here), just a bigger, higher-energy version of the same shape family.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical reasoning: a definite 3D probability-density shape, a boundary that encloses the same fixed fraction of measurements, and the same node-counting rule (angular = l, radial = n − l − 1) — only n and the atom change, never the physics.
